title: Primary color palette
slide_intent: Teach designers to distinguish the colors that identify the movement from those supporting the composition. White space affects how prominently the primary colors appear.
strategic_value: Repeated red and gray can connect core materials such as stationery and signage, with the supporting palette allowing variation.
demonstration: Overlapping labeled circles present red, gray, biscuit and black above a white curved field. Red and gray receive the largest areas and reproduction specifications appear within the swatches.
practical_value: Choose red and gray as the identifying pair for a core communication. Use the supporting colors and the white field to set emphasis.

content_islands.name: Palette rationale
content_islands.spec: Place a bold statement above the swatches identifying the core and supporting roles.

content_islands.name: Primary and supporting swatches
content_islands.spec: Overlap different-sized circles. Keep names and print, screen or paint references with each relevant color.

content_islands.name: White field
content_islands.spec: Use the white ground beneath the curve and a separate left note to make white’s compositional role explicit.
